newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VICENZA READY FOR VENGEFUL JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-VICENZA READY FOR VENGEFUL JUVENTUS.

text.p: Having beaten Juventus twice in a row in serie A, Vicenza are looking to complete the hat-trick on Saturday but fear the numbers may be against them.
"We are coming in with four consecutive away defeats behind us," said attacker Roberto Murgita,
"The odds are not looking good but sooner or later the law of numbers will strike again. It would be great for us to break the negative run against Juventus."
Unfortunately, the same logic applies to Juventus -- who have only lost twice in the league this season, one of them a 2-1 defeat in Vicenza in October.
They lost 2-1 in Vicenza last season too but in the corresponding match at home won 1-0.
Vicenza led the league in November and again briefly in December but things have changed since then and the humble club with some of the lowest salaries in serie A are now seventh.

However they reached the Italian cup final for the first time in their 95 year history this week and that could prove an important morale boost for a side whose main aim is to avoid relegation before they start thinking about qualifying for Europe.

Juventus defender Moreno Torricelli said recently he and his team were looking forward to Saturday's match as a chance to avenge their earlier defeat, when the Turin team dominated the match and still ended up losers.
Former Italian great Paolo Rossi, who played for both clubs in the late 1970s and early 1980s, said earlier this month he thought Juventus would come out on top.
"They lost the away match but that was the best Vicenza, in front of its own fans.
"And Juve lost playing well, at least the equal of the "biancorossi" (white-reds), and for an hour they played better.

"Now (Francesco) Guidolin's team is on the slide and I don't think that at the Delle Alpi, against a Juve already concentrating on the European Cup, much will change. I'm divided between the two, but I think the Torinese are favourites."

Rossi was speaking before the extent of Juventus' injury problem became apparent. Since then Alessandro Del Piero, Alen Boksic, Angelo Peruzzi and Didier Deschamps have all been ruled out, while Zinedine Zidane is serving a one match ban.
Del Piero and Boksic were also absent last time round in October, when Juventus were also reduced to 10 men.

However Juventus still have several Italian internationals in their line-up, including defender Ciro Ferrara and midfielder Angelo Di Livio. The two likely strikers -- Michele Padovano and Christian Viera -- are no slouches either.

Yugoslav Vladimir Jugovic will also play and he is a rarity at Juventus -- a world class player who has won European Cups with both Juve and Red Star Belgrade and yet still remains something of an unknown to many Italians.
If anything, the absence of the regular firepower will encourage Jugovic and Padovano to ever greater heights.
The long-haired 30-year-old Padovano is relishing the chance to shake off the tag of part-time striker and has been a regular since the New Year due to the team's injury problems.
Once rejected by Juventus, the speedy player is a favourite with the fans and has scored several crucial goals.
The pressure on his shoulders will be alleviated by the fact that Juventus are five points clear at the top of the league and will stay comfortably ahead whatever happens on Saturday.
Attilio Lombardo, who won the league with Sampdoria in 1991, should make his third league start of the season for Juventus.
"Of course it won't be the usual Juve against Vicenza," he admitted. "But it won't be a team completely without imagination or invention either.
"Maybe it will be a bit less attractive than usual but we will try to be firm, cynical if we have to be. The main thing is to keep the five point advantage."
